mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across time, making the signal always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precede corporate earnings declines and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates broad-based economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through stronger corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST growth exceeds 0.5% and INDPRO is above 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% and sustained for at least 3 months), the S&P 500 typically underperforms due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising above 0.5% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2.0% (GDPC1) signals robust economic fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through immediate corporate earnings support.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annual inflation rate above 2.5% (CPIAUCSL) indicates rising price pressures that often prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL annual change exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of strong labor market growth (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which typically supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE is below 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (low unemployment and moderate GDP growth), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to valuation pressures and anticipation of monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% and GDPC1 growth between 1.5% and 2.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0% and GDPC1 growth is between 1.5% and 2.5%.
